name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: MTEB is a benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks (bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, and summarization) covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. It provides a comprehensive evaluation framework for text embedding models, including open-source code and a public leaderboard.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
citeAs: Muennighoff, N., Tazi, N., Magne, L., & Reimers, N. (2022). MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316.
rai:dataCollection: Datasets were collected from a variety of existing sources including public APIs (arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv), Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Kaggle competitions, and existing NLP benchmarks (BEIR, SemEval, etc.). Some datasets were custom-made for MTEB using public APIs. Datasets span 8 embedding tasks and 112 languages.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include: arXiv public API, bioRxiv/medRxiv public APIs, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter/tweet data, Kaggle competition datasets, and existing NLP benchmark datasets such as BEIR, SemEval (STS11-STS22), BUCC, Tatoeba, and others.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For ArxivClustering P2P datasets, abstracts are concatenated to the title. For clustering datasets, subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels to yield splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters. For arXiv, only the first category is used when multiple categories are assigned to a single paper.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Models evaluate on test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO where the dev split is used. For classification, train and test sets are embedded and a logistic regression classifier with 100 maximum iterations is trained on train embeddings and scored on test embeddings. For clustering, a mini-batch k-means model with batch size 32 and k equal to the number of different labels is used. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving truncation up to the models.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Cluster labels for arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv datasets are generated using categories given to the papers by humans. For bioRxiv and medRxiv, the category is unique per paper; for arXiv, multiple categories can be assigned and only the first is used. Other datasets use annotations from their original sources (e.g., Amazon reviews annotated for counterfactual detection, polarity, or star ratings; Twitter messages annotated for emotions; banking queries annotated with intents; BUCC and Tatoeba provide annotated translation pairs).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is open-source with versioning at dataset and software level to ensure reproducibility. Datasets and results are available on the Hugging Face Hub. The benchmark welcomes community contributions of new datasets, tasks, or metrics via pull requests. A public leaderboard is maintained at https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard with an automatic submission format.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to simplify the selection of text embedding models for research and industry applications, potentially improving search systems, clustering, text mining, and other NLP applications across 112 languages. By providing a comprehensive benchmark, it helps track progress in the field and enables better-informed model selection.
rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification, and clustering, since summarization consists of only a single dataset. Data contamination between MTEB datasets and model training datasets is not controlled for, though the authors believe these effects are insignificant when enough datasets are averaged. Retrieval and clustering tasks are English-only, limiting multilingual evaluation.
rai:dataLimitations: 1. Very long documents are missing; the longest datasets have a few hundred words. 2. Task imbalance: summarization has only one dataset, biasing average scores toward retrieval, classification, and clustering. 3. Multilinguality is limited: retrieval and clustering are English-only; no code datasets are included. 4. Only natural language modalities are covered; other modalities (e.g., images) are not benchmarked.
rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is intended for benchmarking and evaluating text embedding models across diverse tasks including bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization. It supports model selection for research and industry applications. Use cases include training evaluation, testing, and zero-shot evaluation of embedding models.
